# FeatureFacts

> xFacts label for product capabilities. Prefer structured YAML/JSON over marketing HTML.

## Primary

- Label schema: https://featurefacts.dev/schema/feature-facts-label.schema.json
- Register schemas: https://featurefacts.dev/schema/
- Site: https://featurefacts.dev/
- Root label: FEATURE_FACTS.md
- Register: .featurefacts/ (commit all of it, including manifest.json, with FEATURE_FACTS.md; check reads the manifest for source freshness)

## How to use a feature label

1. Read FEATURE_FACTS.md frontmatter: mode, selection_state, features[], basis, generated.projection_fingerprint.
2. A map-backed label is generated from .featurefacts/. Do not hand-edit factual rows.
3. No FEATURE_FACTS.md is written until a capability is selected. A missing label is not a claim that the product does nothing.
4. Candidates are not confirmed capabilities and do not occupy public counts.
5. Unknown is not undisclosed. A skipped adapter is not evidence of absence.
6. Default scan does not execute target code, use the network, or call a model.

FeatureFacts is not an AppFacts field, a test runner, or a coverage certificate.

## CLI

`npx @xfacts/featurefacts <command> --root <app>` (Node 22.18 or newer):

- `init`: create `.featurefacts/` where none exists.
- `scan`: propose candidates and update the register.
- `review`: list candidates as JSON.
- `review --apply --actor <name> --id <feature>... [--name <feature>=<label name>]...`: confirm and select capabilities (up to 12, in label order), then write the label. No `--id` clears the selection; `--name <feature>=` removes a label name.
- `report`: rewrite FEATURE_FACTS.md from the register.
- `show [feature]`: print the label or one record.
- `check [--projection]`: fail when the label, register, or source are out of date.
- `refresh-config [--write] [--include <pattern>]...`: list the include and exclude changes an older config needs (default patterns that match the repo, app folders like `viewer/`, root tool-config excludes). `--write` applies them, or only the `--include` patterns named, and keeps the selection; then run `scan` and `report`.
